{"Title": "Evaluation of the WHO Special Programme on Primary Health Care: Report - BRIEF_ SP PHC Evaluation 28 Feb.pdf", "Abstract": "**Summary:**\n\nThe World Health Organization's (WHO) Special Programme on Primary Health Care (SP-PHC) was established in 2020 to improve the integration of the Primary Health Care (PHC) approach within WHO. An evaluation of SP-PHC was conducted to assess its effectiveness in supporting WHO PHC objectives and make recommendations for the future towards universal health coverage (UHC). The evaluation found that SP-PHC has raised substantial external and WHO core resources but lacks a well-defined strategy, theory of change, and programme-wide work plan. The report highlights the need for a clear strategy to promote PHC through global advocacy, policy, and strategic partnerships.\n\nThe evaluation also identified several challenges and limitations, including uneven relationships with other WHO departments, managerial complexities, and a lack of PHC-specific progress indicators and targets. The report recommends overhauling the SP-PHC design, organizational structure, and ways of working to ensure the new entity is fit for purpose to implement the strategy. Additionally, the report suggests developing a transition plan for existing work units, creating mechanisms for learning, staff capacity-building, and flexible support for PHC through technical assistance rosters and directories of PHC expertise.\n\nThe evaluation concludes that while SP-PHC has added value globally through its advocacy function and normative products, there is a need to shift towards a more facilitative, service-oriented, and collaborative approach. The report emphasizes the importance of promoting PHC through global advocacy, policy, and strategic partnerships to accelerate progress towards UHC.\n\n**Main Topics:**\n\n1. **Primary Health Care (PHC)**: The evaluation focuses on the WHO's Special Programme on Primary Health Care (SP-PHC) and its role in promoting PHC within WHO.\n2. **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)**: The evaluation aims to assess the effectiveness of SP-PHC in supporting WHO PHC objectives and making recommendations for the future towards UHC.\n3. **Programme Evaluation**: The evaluation is conducted to assess the effectiveness of SP-PHC and make recommendations for improvement.\n4. **Organizational Development**: The report highlights the need for a clear strategy, theory of change, and programme-wide work plan to ensure the effectiveness of SP-PHC.\n5. **Global Health Policy**: The evaluation emphasizes the importance of promoting PHC through global advocacy, policy, and strategic partnerships.\n\n**Key Terms & Concepts:**\n\n1. **Primary Health Care (PHC)**: A holistic approach to health care that focuses on preventing and treating diseases at the community level.\n2. **Universal Health Coverage (UHC)**: A global health goal that aims to ensure that all individuals have access to essential health services without facing financial hardship.\n3. **Theory of Change**: initiative.\n5. **Global Advocacy**: The use of advocacy efforts to promote a cause or issue at the global level.\n6. **Policy Partnerships**: Collaborations between organizations to promote policy {"Title": "Evaluation of WFP\u2019s Emergency Preparedness Policy (2017) - Evaluation Report (from special page)", "Abstract": "**Summary:**\n\nThe evaluation report assesses the effectiveness of the World Food Programme's (WFP) Emergency Preparedness Policy (2017). risk analysis, and strong partnerships.\n5. **Efficiency and Effectiveness**: The need for robust evidence on the effects of preparedness, limited efforts to integrate gender and disability inclusion, {"Title": "Evaluation of WFP\u2019s Emergency Preparedness Policy (2017) - Evaluation Report (from special page)", "Abstract": "**Summary:**\n\nThe World Food Programme (WFP) conducted an evaluation of its Emergency Preparedness Policy (2017) to assess its effectiveness and identify areas for improvement. A formative evaluation of the GHC highlights both its successes and areas for improvement. The report emphasizes the need for the GHC to prioritize and adjust to the humanitarian reset, focusing on core functions and essential support.
